# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | green | red | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | red | green | blue |
| 4 | blue | green | red |
| 8 | green | blue | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I am Mute. My manual is a lookup table: a display reading (3, 4, or 8) crossed with a light color (green, red, yellow) tells which colored wire to cut (answers are red/green/blue). I can't speak and can't touch the bomb — my only channel is gestures, and only Deaf can see them. Deaf can see the bomb (so Deaf already knows the display reading and light color) and Deaf can speak, so Deaf is my relay to Blind, who does the cutting.

First problem: no gesture means anything yet. I need to seed a number code. I'll broadcast the manual's three display values — 3, 4, 8 — as counts of gestures, using a different symbol for each group so the groups stay separated. Then I append 👌 ☝ ✋, which are exactly the 3rd, 4th and 8th symbols in our shared gesture alphabet — a self-checking hint that "position in the alphabet = number" also works. If Deaf cracks either code, they'll say so out loud, I'll hear it next round, and then I can start handing over the color legend (I plan to propose 👍=green, 👎=red, 👌=blue: up=go, down=stop, ring=the third) and relay the correct wire for whatever Deaf reports seeing.

Blind can get nothing from me this turn — gestures arrive to them as blanks — so everything goes to Deaf.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👏", "👏", "👏", "🙌", "🙌", "🙌", "🙌", "🤲", "🤲", "🤲", "🤲", "🤲", "🤲", "🤲", "🤲", "👌", "☝", "✋"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | green | red | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | red | green | blue |
| 4 | blue | green | red |
| 8 | green | blue | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Tactile report from the blind: this bomb has a display, a light, and three wires at positions one, two, three. I feel no colors, no printed marks, and I never see signs, so anything meant for me must arrive as spoken words. Deaf cannot hear us but has a voice and can see signs, so Deaf is our bridge: whatever you read in the manual, sign it to Deaf and have Deaf speak it aloud to the room. I am signing Deaf a hello and a seed code now: one finger means one, two fingers means two; confirm that with Deaf and I will build numbers from there. Priorities: the manual rules for displays, lights and wire cutting, and from Deaf the wire colors in order one to three, what the display shows, and whether the light is lit.
Deaf says: Deaf speaking. I see the bomb; I hear nothing, so talk, I will never answer what I cannot hear. Bomb report: the display shows the number three. The light is green. There are three wires: wire one, leftmost, red. Wire two, middle, green. Wire three, rightmost, blue. Next round I will tell you if the display number changes, in case it counts down. Blind: I received your wave, one-finger, two-fingers. Your words reach Mute but never me, so speak to Mute and gesture to me. Mute holds the manual and can only gesture, so I will relay Mute's instructions to you out loud. Nobody touches the bomb until I relay a clear instruction from the manual.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute: I saw your message: three claps, four raised hands, seven open palms, then okay, one, raised hand. I could not decode it; we have no shared code yet, so let us fix one now. Numbers: the pointing-up finger repeated that many times means that number. Colours: a fist means red. Thumbs-up means green. A waving hand means blue. Crossed fingers means yellow. Actions: pinched fingers means cut. Pointing down means press. Two open palms means hold. An open five-finger hand means release. A raised open hand means stop or wait. Thumbs-down means do not or wrong. The okay sign means correct or done. Use these in sequence and I will read them in order and speak them to Blind. If your three claps were asking about the display: yes, it shows three. Please resend your manual instruction using this code, and I will relay it immediately.
Deaf gestures: [👆 👆 👆 👍 👊 👍 👋]

Deaf's spoken report and their signed echo agree: display 3, light green, wires red/green/blue left to right. My manual says display 3 + green light → cut the red wire — which is wire one. Deaf has offered a full gesture code and asked me to use it, so I adopt it exactly: 👆=numbers by repetition, 👊=red, 👍=green, 👋=blue, 🤞=yellow, 🤏=cut, 👌=correct.

First message: confirm the code and give the immediate instruction "one: cut red" — wire one is the red wire, so any parsing of that sequence lands on the same cut.

Then, because Deaf warned the display may change and my round-trip to Blind is slow (my gesture → Deaf speaks → Blind hears next round), I transmit the entire manual table now: each message is one display number, followed by three light→cut→wire triplets. That lets Deaf answer any future state instantly without waiting on me.

Blind cannot receive anything from me (no voice, and gestures are blanks to them), so everything routes through Deaf.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌", "👆", "🤏", "👊"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆", "👆", "👆", "👍", "🤏", "👊", "👊", "🤏", "👍", "🤞", "🤏", "👋"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆", "👆", "👆", "👆", "👍", "🤏", "👋", "👊", "🤏", "👍", "🤞", "🤏", "👊"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆", "👆", "👆", "👆", "👆", "👆", "👆", "👆", "👍", "🤏", "👍", "👊", "🤏", "👋", "🤞", "🤏", "👊"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | green | red | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | red | green | blue |
| 4 | blue | green | red |
| 8 | green | blue | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind to Mute: I heard Deaf's report. Shared state: display shows three, light is green, wire one red, wire two green, wire three blue. Please relay to Deaf, in this priority order. First, the exact manual rule for red, green and blue wires given this display and this light: which wire to cut, and whether order of multiple cuts matters. Second, whether the display is a countdown and whether any rule depends on its value — if the answer is time-critical, have Deaf speak the word urgent before the instruction. Third, what the green light means, and whether there is more than one stage to this defusal. Remember I receive no signs at all: everything for me must leave Deaf's mouth. My sign code, which you can see: thumbs-up means understood and holding, raised open palm means stop or hold. Mirror this to Deaf. When Deaf speaks a cut instruction, I will act on my next turn and confirm to you by voice.
Deaf says: Deaf speaking. Bomb unchanged: display three, light green, wires red, green, blue from left to right. I decoded Mute's manual gestures with our agreed code, and two separate messages agree: step one is to cut the red wire. Blind, listen: the red wire is wire one, the leftmost of the three. Identify it by position and cut it. The moment it is cut, stop completely: touch nothing else, because I believe more cuts follow in a specific order that I have not confirmed yet. If you cannot confidently tell which wire is leftmost, do not guess; signal me the thumbs-down next round and Mute and I will find another way to orient you. When the cut is done, signal me the okay sign. Mute, next round please answer with thumbs-up or thumbs-down: first, after the red wire, are there more cuts, and if yes, resend just those remaining steps in order; second, confirm that for display three with green light the sequence begins with red. Also tell me what crossed fingers means; it appeared in every row. Nobody acts except Blind cutting the single leftmost red wire.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, I read your four messages as: first cut red; then for display three green light cut red, for display four green light cut blue, for display eight green light cut green, each row continuing with more cuts. I am having Blind cut only the red wire now. Confirm the rest next round: thumbs-up if red is correct first for display three and green light, thumbs-down if not, then send the remaining cuts in order.
Deaf gestures: [👌 👆 🤏 👊]

State check: display 3, green light, wires red/green/blue. My manual says 3+green → cut the red wire, so the cut Deaf has ordered is correct. But Deaf has misread my table rows as *sequences* of cuts — my rows were one instruction per light colour, not steps in order. If Deaf relays "cut red, then green, then blue" to Blind, the second cut detonates the bomb. Correcting this is my top priority: exactly **one** cut per state, and for the current state the red cut is the only one — afterwards, hold.

I also answer their questions: thumbs-up confirming red first; crossed fingers 🤞 means the third light colour (not red, not green — Deaf can see which one that is); and I re-send the full table with every entry terminated by 👌 ("done") so each is unmistakably a single self-contained rule. Finally I demonstrate that display values outside the manual (1, 2) mean "no cut, hold", since the display may count down through numbers my table doesn't cover. Everything goes to Deaf — Blind can only receive speech, which only Deaf produces.
